newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE sets up voting programme for Bosnians abroad.
newsitem.headline: OSCE sets up voting programme for Bosnians abroad.

text.p: Europe's top security forum said on Tuesday it had set up a special programme to enable citizens of Bosnia living abroad to vote in the September local elections.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said it had established the "Out-of-Country-Program" with the International Organisation for Migration to register and prepare voting procedures for Bosnians abroad.
Some one million Bosnians fled their homeland as a result of the 43-month conflict in the region.
The OSCE is charged with supervising Bosnia's elections, set for September 13 and 14, under the terms of the Dayton peace accord that ended the war in 1995.

Bosnians residing in more than 50 countries will be able to register between May 5 and June 7 by absentee ballot or in person. All Bosnians over the age of 18 who are included in a 1991 census may vote.

The local polls are viewed as Bosnia's last chance for reunification because they should enable refugees to cross over to their former homes and cast votes, reversing the results of the war's ethnic cleansing.
